excerpts.text: * An estimated 282 million new malaria cases in 80 endemic countries worldwide in 2024, up from 273 million in 2023.
* Ten countries account for 66% of all malaria cases worldwide: Nigeria, DRC, Uganda, Ethiopia, Mozambique, Angola, Tanzania, Cote d’Ivoire, Mali and Burkina Faso.

* The WHO Africa Region accounts for 94% of cases and 95% of deaths globally.
* Three countries – Nigeria (31.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (11.7%) and Niger (6.1%) – accounted for half of all deaths in the region.

excerpts.text: East Africa carries a disproportionate share of the global malaria burden, with the WHO African Region accounting for 94% of global malaria cases and 95% of malaria deaths by 2023 [19]. In East Africa, Uganda accounts for 5.1% of global malaria cases and 2.9% of global deaths, representing the highest proportion in East Africa (23%) [19, 20].
Ethiopia accounts for 3.6% of global malaria cases with over 7.3 million cases reported in 2024 and 1157 deaths (CFR 0.02%) [23].
The World Health Organization reported an estimated 249 million malaria cases globally by 2023, of which 94% occurred in Africa, with Tanzania being one of the high-burden countries [25].
